title: Florida House, District 73
what_it_does: Represents District 73 (Part of Sarasota) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings.

candidates.name: Fiona McFarland
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: State representative for District 73 since 2020; U.S. Navy Reserve officer; former McKinsey consultant
candidates.background: Sarasota-area Republican first elected in 2020. A 2008 U.S. Naval Academy graduate, she served eight years on active duty as a surface warfare officer and remains in the Navy Reserve; she holds an MBA from UNC Kenan-Flagler and consulted at McKinsey and Company. She lives in Venice with her husband and child.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

property_tax.summary: Voted yes on HJR 1-F in the June 2026 special session, which placed Amendment 3 on the November ballot to raise the homestead exemption for non-school property taxes to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028 and to limit how counties and cities may spend property-tax revenue.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, CS/HJR 1F (Save our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes), passage 75-26

immigration.summary: Voted yes on SB 2-C (2025), which created the State Board of Immigration Enforcement, required state help with federal detainers, barred driver licenses for unauthorized immigrants, and funded an Unauthorized Alien Transport Program.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, SB 2-C (Immigration), passage 85-30

guns.summary: Voted yes on HB 543 (2023), which allows carrying a concealed firearm without a state license.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, CS/HB 543 (concealed carry without a license), passage 76-32

education_choice.summary: Voted yes on HB 1 (2023), which removed income limits and enrollment caps so state scholarship funds can follow any K-12 student to private or home education.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, CS/CS/CS/CS/HB 1 (universal school-choice scholarships), passage 83-27

candidates.name: Lisa Klein
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Licensed mental health counselor; private-practice owner; former educator
candidates.background: Longtime Florida resident and Sarasota-based licensed mental health counselor who owns a private practice, formerly worked as an educator and is a mother. She describes advocacy for disability rights and school accountability after her family faced discrimination in the school system.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

insurance.summary: She said that in her first six months she would push for strict caps on property-insurance rate hikes, clearer justification requirements for rate increases, stronger policyholder protections, and more home-hardening grants.
insurance.quote: I will advocate for strict caps on rate hikes, legislation requiring clearer justifications for proposed insurance rate hikes, and stronger protections for policyholders.

sources.title: VOTE411 (League of Women Voters) 2026 general election guide, State Representative 73 (candidate's own answers; accessed Oct. 7, 2026)

abortion.summary: She supports access to IVF, contraception and abortion and said she would work to end Florida's abortion ban.
abortion.quote: I will fight to end Florida's abortion ban because decisions about if, when, and how to start or grow a family should be free from government overreach.

sources.title: VOTE411 (League of Women Voters) 2026 general election guide, State Representative 73 (candidate's own answers; accessed Oct. 7, 2026)

healthcare.summary: She supports Medicaid expansion and state premium help for Marketplace enrollees who lose federal subsidies, along with more support for community health centers.
healthcare.quote: we must start by drawing down available federal healthcare dollars through Medicaid expansion.

sources.title: VOTE411 (League of Women Voters) 2026 general election guide, State Representative 73 (candidate's own answers; accessed Oct. 7, 2026)
Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, Lisa Klein (submitted July 14, 2026)

education_choice.summary: She would restore an income limit for school vouchers and add fiscal-transparency oversight of voucher schools, while pushing for fully funded public schools.
education_choice.quote: I will propose restoring an income eligibility limit for school vouchers, institute oversight measures for voucher schools, including fiscal transparency, and fight for fully funded public schools.

sources.title: VOTE411 (League of Women Voters) 2026 general election guide, State Representative 73 (candidate's own answers; accessed Oct. 7, 2026)

housing.summary: She backs state incentives tied to long-term affordable units, a statewide Tenant Bill of Rights, eviction-diversion programs, limits on rental application fees and state support for community land trusts.
housing.quote: For renters, I will advocate for local eviction-diversion programs, reasonable limits on rental application fees, and a statewide Tenant Bill of Rights with clear protections for fair lease practices.

sources.title: VOTE411 (League of Women Voters) 2026 general election guide, State Representative 73 (candidate's own answers; accessed Oct. 7, 2026)

growth.summary: She said laws such as the Live Local Act and SB 180 limit local decisions on growth and zoning, and she supports restoring home rule over local planning and development.
growth.quote: I support restoring home rule over local planning and development.

sources.title: VOTE411 (League of Women Voters) 2026 general election guide, State Representative 73 (candidate's own answers; accessed Oct. 7, 2026)

elections.summary: If proof of citizenship were required to register, she would have the state check records it already holds, waive document fees, and create an appeal process for name mismatches.
elections.quote: Citizenship rules must never turn a paperwork problem into the loss of an eligible citizen's vote.

sources.title: VOTE411 (League of Women Voters) 2026 general election guide, State Representative 73 (candidate's own answers; accessed Oct. 7, 2026)

crime.summary: Among her first-term priorities she listed funding for local crisis-response and diversion programs. She did not address criminal penalties or police budgets directly.
crime.quote: I will also seek funding for local crisis-response and diversion programs and support Medicaid expansion.

sources.title: VOTE411 (League of Women Voters) 2026 general election guide, State Representative 73 (candidate's own answers; accessed Oct. 7, 2026)

other_issues.title: Affordability, education oversight and mental health
other_issues.summary: Klein says she is running to fight for working individuals and families and to build what she calls a healthier, more affordable Florida, with an emphasis on rising household costs, disability rights, school accountability and access to mental health care. Her campaign site describes her approach as evidence-based but does not set out positions on specific bills.
